sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned Special Public Prosecutor for the State.
Despite service of notice on respondent No.2, no one has entered appearance to oppose the prayer.
2. The trial court records have been placed before this Court to consider the prayer of the appellant for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 376 and 504 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'the IPC') and Section 4 of the Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1237 of 2024(12) dt.25-02-2026 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the POCSO Act'), vide judgment dated 09.09.2024 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI- cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Madhepura, in POCSO Case No. 11 of 2019, arising out of Udakishunganj P.S. Case No. 63 of 2019,

sentences.text: The prosecution case is based on a written information submitted by father of the victim girl on 21.02.2019 alleging that when his daughter ('X') was alone in her house, on 19.02.2019, at about 12 noon, the appellant entered into his house and finding the victim girl alone, he gagged her mouth and committed rape on her, he also gave teeth bites at several places of the victim's body.

He claimed that when he came back from the market and his wife came back her home, then the victim disclosed the occurrence, whereafter he went to the accused and asked him as to why he has committed this Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1237 of 2024(12) dt.25-02-2026 occurrence.
It is alleged that the accused started threatening that if you would lodge a case, then he would kill the entire family.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the present case is out and out a case of false implication of the appellant for the purpose of usurping his land.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that it would appear that the victim was not examined under Section 164 CrPC., she has stated in her deposition that she had no land and in the present case her father had filed a compromise petition.

It is pointed out that the victim was specifically asked as to whether the house,
in which she was residing, is situated on the land of Fareed (the appellant), the victim admitted that the land belongs to the appellant.
She also admitted that the land has not been sold by the appellant to her father.

6. Learned counsel submits that the deposition of the victim (PW 1) clearly demonstrates that the victim and her family have occupied the land of this appellant and because of the said land, which she is unauthorizedly occupying, and the appellant wanted to get the same vacated, the present case has been lodged after alleging the occurrence.

It is also pointed out from the evidence of PW 2 that he had disclosed the age of his daughter as 17 years on the date of the occurrence, but the Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1237 of 2024(12) dt.25-02-2026 mother of the victim (PW 3)
has stated that her daughter was aged 19 years at the time of occurrence, but she cannot say the date of birth.

7. Learned counsel submits that the Doctor (PW 4) opined on the basis of bone ossification test of the victim that she was between 15 and 17 years, even if this is taken into consideration, by giving plus minus two years of benefit, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajak Mohammad vs. State of H.P., reported in (2018) 9 SCC 248, the upper extremity of the age of the victim would come to 19 years, therefore, the charges under the POCSO Act is also likely to fail in ultimate analysis.

entities.text: Rajak Mohammad vs. State of H.P., reported in (2018) 9 SCC 248
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel further submits that the victim was examined by Doctor Alka Kumari (PW 4) in the Sadar Hospital and Dr. Kumar Anupam, who was one of the members of the board, and the Doctors have opined that there was no external or internal injury on the person of the victim.

The Doctor has opined in her cross-examination that the victim had not mentioned of any complain regarding external injury and further it is recorded that no recent sign of rape was found on the private part of the victim.

9. It is submitted that when the IO (PW 5) has stated Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1237 of 2024(12) dt.25-02-2026 in his evidence that he had not found any special marks/sign at the place of Md. Fareed vs The State Of Bihar on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160492938/
2 occurrence and had not taken the victim for her statement under Section 164 CrPC.

entities.text: Md. Fareed vs The State Of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The IO has affirmed that the age of the appellant is 70-72 years and prior to the occurrence, there was no complaint against him.
10. The prayer of the appellant has been opposed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.
It is submitted that even as it appears that there is some dispute with respect to the land on which the victim claims her house, it is evident that the victim has supported her case.

11. Having regard to the entire facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence, which we have prima facie gone through, at this stage, for the purpose of consideration of the prayer of the appellant, we have noticed that in this case the upper extremity of the age of the victim is to be assessed as 19 years in absence of any other proof of age in terms of the scheme of Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, her mother (PW 3) has clearly opined that the victim was aged 19 years on the date of occurrence, this Court has further noticed that the claim of the victim that the appellant had committed rape on her and he had given several teeth bites stands fully falsified from the medical Patna High Court CR.

dt.25-02-2026 examination report as neither any external injury has been found on her body nor the Doctor has opined any sign of recent sexual act on her

, this Court further noticed that the victim admits that her house is on the land of the appellant and she further admits that in this case a compromise has been filed, the false implication of the appellant cannot be ruled out, at this stage,
and there are palpable materials for this Court to take a view that the appellant deserves suspension of sentence and release on bail during pendency of this appeal.

Accordingly, we direct suspension of his sentence and release on bail during pendency of the appeal on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VI- cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Madhepura, in POCSO Case No. 11 of 2019, arising out of Udakishunganj P.S. Case No. 63 of 2019.
12.
